subject: Embed onboarding: cutover readiness + rerank sample plan
messages:
From: Emma Rodriguez <emma@acmecommerce.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Embeddings kickoff + quick questions about backfill

Hi Tessa and Monica,

Thanks again for the quick demo yesterday — excited to get moving. We want to make sure the first-week handoff focuses on the minimum work to make rerank stable in production. A few quick items from our side: 

- Estimated index size: ~8M documents, average doc length ~450 tokens.
- Current store: PostgreSQL with precomputed text columns.
- We expect a 72-hour backfill window is acceptable if it does not impact live traffic.

Can you confirm:
1) Recommended vector DB for a hosted Redwood deployment vs our on-prem evaluation?
2) Best approach for incremental backfills so we can continue writes to the primary DB?
3) Suggested size of the rerank eval set and how Redwood wants to handle human review for the first pass?

I can make time for a quick call tomorrow afternoon. Attaching our sample queries and a short export of the current primary keys.

Thanks,
Emma
Customer ML Lead
Acme Commerce

Attachments: sample-queries.csv, primary-keys-export.csv

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Rodriguez <emma@acmecommerce.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-03T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings kickoff + quick questions about backfill

Hi Emma — great to hear and thanks for the export. Quick answers up front, then a proposed first-week plan below: 

1) Vector DB recs: for hosted customers we generally recommend a managed vector store (Pinecone or a managed Redis Vector store) for low operational overhead. For on-prem/private we typically advise Faiss with persistent snapshotting or Redis Vector if the ops team can support it. I put pros/cons in the checklist.

2) Backfill approach: do an initial snapshot backfill to the vector DB in a read-only staging index, validate rerank scores, then swap the index via alias to minimize live impact. For continuous writes use an incremental worker that processes CDC events and updates vectors; we can provide a small connector template.

3) Rerank eval set: start with 1k labeled queries covering the top 10 intents. Use automated metrics (nDCG@5, MRR@10) and a human review sample of 200 results for quality checks.

Proposed first-week checkpoints (we can adjust during the call):
- Day 1: Confirm vector DB choice + credentials and access.
- Day 2: Wire up connector and run a 100k seed backfill to staging.
- Day 3-4: Run rerank evals against the staging index, iterate on candidate filters.
- Day 5: Production alias cutover with rollback window and monitoring.

I attached a short onboarding-checklist.xlsx with tasks and owners. Would you be available 8/4 at 3pm PT for a 30-minute sync?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: onboarding-checklist.xlsx

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Rodriguez <emma@acmecommerce.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-04T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings kickoff + quick questions about backfill

Thanks Emma and Tessa — joining the 3pm PT call. A few operational notes I want to capture here so we have alignment before the sync: 

- Indexing speed: with an optimized pipeline we typically see 50-200k vectors/hour depending on embedding model and batch sizing. For 8M docs we should plan a staged backfill over multiple workers or a burst window.
- Safety & dedupe: recommend a pre-processing step to dedupe by canonical URL/id and normalize whitespace/tokenization. We should also flag and remove PII during staging.
- Consistency: use an index alias for zero-downtime swap and keep the old index for 48 hours for quick rollback.
- Cost ops: if you choose Pinecone, expect ~30% faster vector upserts than self-hosted Faiss but higher monthly cost; we'll include a cost estimate in the follow-up.

Deliverables we'll produce in week 1:
- seed-backfill-runbook.md (includes commands and failure recovery)
- sample-queries.csv (you provided) + expanded query set for eval
- acceptance-criteria.md (pass/fail thresholds for nDCG/MRR and human sampling plan)
- monitoring dashboard link (will share post-call)

I'll bring the runbook and acceptance criteria to the call. If you can upload credentials to the Drive link ahead of the meeting that will speed things up.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sample-queries.csv, acceptance-criteria.md

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Emma Rodriguez <emma@acmecommerce.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T13:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings kickoff + quick questions about backfill

Addendum from engineering side on rerank evaluation and technical constraints: 

- Embedding model: recommend starting with text-embedding-3-small for throughput, then evaluate text-embedding-3-large for quality if needed. Batch size tuning will be critical; aim for 128-512 depending on GPU memory for bulk upserts.
- Indexing strategy: run an initial bulk upsert to a staging index using 32 parallel workers with backpressure and exponential retry. Use protobuf or ndjson for upload payloads.
- Incremental updates: use an idempotent upsert and maintain a change-log table to avoid double-processing. We will provide a connector that reads CDC and writes to the vector DB.
- Rerank eval plan:
  * Gold set size: 1,000 queries with a mix of head and tail intents.
  * Metrics: nDCG@5, MRR@10, Recall@100.
  * Human review: 200 sampled queries split across at least 3 annotators to control bias. Use pairwise A/B where possible.
  * Baseline: current TF-IDF retrieval + model rerank. Evaluate relative uplift and failure modes (hallucination, truncation).

I'll drop a runnable notebook for you after the call: rerank-eval-notebook.ipynb with an example scoring pipeline and plotting utilities. Also note warm-start considerations: keep original vectors in case we need to roll back and run incremental diffs.

—Karthik
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
